'''Justin Oliver Harper''' (born August 30, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Utsunomiya Brex]] of the Japanese [[B. League]]. Harper played professionally in the [[NBA]] for various teams, including the [[Orlando Magic]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|University of Richmond]].

==College career==
As a senior with [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]], Harper averaged 17.9 points and 6.9 rebounds while shooting 53 percent from the field, and he was named to the first-team All-[[Atlantic 10]], along with teammate [[Kevin Anderson (basketball)|Kevin Anderson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2010-11all-conferencehonors |title=2010–11 Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams |format=PDF |work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] |access-date=March 23, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110314174055/http://www.atlantic10.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2010-11all-conferencehonors |archive-date=March 14, 2011 }}</ref> Harper was recognized as an All-Fourth District first-team selection by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nabc.org/photos/schools/nabc/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/D1AllDistrict2011.pdf|publisher=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]|title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces 2011 Division I All-District Teams|access-date=March 23, 2011|date=March 9, 2011|archive-date=July 26, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726061719/http://www.nabc.org/photos/schools/nabc/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/D1AllDistrict2011.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Harper was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], who subsequently traded his draft rights to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/06/24/magic.draft.trade.ap/index.html|title=Magic make a trade, selection on draft night|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=June 24, 2011|access-date=June 24, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627232724/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/06/24/magic.draft.trade.ap/index.html|archive-date=June 27, 2011}}</ref> During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Harper played in France for [[SIG Strasbourg]] of the [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 16, 2011 |title=Magic Rookie Justin Harper to Play for France's SIG Strasbourg |url=https://www.slamonline.com/news/nba/magic-rookie-justin-harper-to-play-for-frances-sig-strasbourg |access-date=September 10, 2023 |work=SlamOnline.com}}</ref> On December 9, 2011, he signed with the Magic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news_rookies_120911.html|title=Magic Sign Rookies Harper and Liggins|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref> On October 27, 2012, he was waived by the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2012/10/27/magic-waive-quentin-richardson-justin-harper-and-chris-johnson/|title=Magic waive Quentin Richardson, Justin Harper and Chris Johnson|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=October 27, 2012|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref>

On November 2, 2012, Harper was selected by the [[Idaho Stampede]] with the third overall pick in the [[2012 NBA Development League draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/index.html |title=2012 NBA D-League Draft |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=November 2, 2012 |access-date=September 18, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105044827/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/index.html |archive-date=November 5, 2012 }}</ref> He played in 48 games for Idaho in 2012–13, averaging 11.7 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.

On October 5, 2013, Harper signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of Israel for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 5, 2013 |title=Hapoel Tel Aviv announced Justin Harper |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/106673/hapoel-tel-aviv-announced-justin-harper.html |url-status=dead |access-date=October 5, 2013 |work=Sportando.com |archive-date=October 19, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019064711/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/106673/hapoel-tel-aviv-announced-justin-harper.html }}</ref> On September 10, 2014, he signed with [[Sidigas Avellino]] of Italy for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 10, 2014 |title=Scandone Avellino announces Justin Harper |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/134261/scandone-avellino-announces-justin-harper.html |url-status=dead |access-date=September 11, 2014 |work=Sportando.com |archive-date=September 11, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140911215823/http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/134261/scandone-avellino-announces-justin-harper.html }}</ref>

On September 18, 2015, Harper signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sapp |first=Demetris |date=September 18, 2015 |title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN JUSTIN HARPER |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-sign-justin-harper |access-date=September 18, 2015 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Nets on October 26 after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-waive-harper-and-jones|title=BROOKLYN NETS WAIVE HARPER AND JONES|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 26, 2015|access-date=October 26, 2015}}</ref> On November 16, he was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the D-League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5070970|title=D-Fenders Acquire Justin Harper|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 16, 2015|access-date=November 16, 2015}}</ref> The following day, he made his debut for the D-Fenders in a 114–105 win over the [[Bakersfield Jam]], recording seven points and one rebound in 13 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151117/LADBAK/|title=D-Fenders Pull Away From Jam, 114–105|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 17, 2015|access-date=November 17, 2015|archive-date=November 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121021711/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151117/LADBAK/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 29, 2016, he was named in the West All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Sixteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016|archive-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207115139/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 24, 2016, Harper signed a 10-day contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 24, 2016 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Forward Justin Harper to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-forward-justin-harper-10-day-contract |access-date=February 24, 2016 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> That night, he made his debut for the Pistons in a 111–91 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], recording one point and one steal in five minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hogg |first=Dave |date=February 24, 2016 |title=Harris leads balanced offense as Pistons rout 76ers |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/PHIDET/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160228082612/http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/PHIDET/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 28, 2016 |access-date=February 28, 2016 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> On March 5, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 5, 2016 |title=Pistons sign Justin Harper to second 10-day contract |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/03/05/pistons-sign-justin-harper-second-10-day-contract/81363782 |access-date=September 10, 2023 |work=DetroitNews.com}}</ref> On March 15, the Pistons decided not to sign him for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Brudenell|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/03/15/detroit-pistons-stan-van-gundy/81823724/|title=Detroit Pistons' Stan Van Gundy still furious the day after loss|date=March 15, 2016|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|access-date=March 15, 2016}}</ref> He subsequently returned to the D-Fenders and played out the rest of the 2016–17 season with them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 21, 2016 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321233946/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=March 21, 2016 }}</ref>

Harper re-joined the D-Fenders for the 2016–17 season. On March 3, 2017, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[2016–17 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-sign-justin-harper-10-day-contract|title=Sixers Sign Justin Harper To 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 3, 2017}}</ref> After the 10-day contract expired, Harper was reacquired by the D-Fenders.<ref>{{cite web |last=Greene |first=T.C. |date=March 13, 2017 |title=Los Angeles Reacquires Justin Harper |url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/los-angeles-reacquires-justin-harper/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318010805/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/los-angeles-reacquires-justin-harper/ |archive-date=March 18, 2017 |access-date=March 17, 2017 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

Harper re-joined the D-Fenders, this time re-branded as the South Bay Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Camarena|first1=Noah|title=South Bay Lakers acquire Justin Harper|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-justin-harper/|website=NBA G League|access-date=December 4, 2018|date=December 4, 2018|archive-date=December 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181205060701/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-justin-harper/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 25, 2019, Harper joined [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orriola |first=Verónica |date=April 25, 2019 |title=Sale Tyrone Curnell entra Justin Harper como refuerzo de los Indios |url=https://magazine-pr.com/sale-tyrone-curnell-entra-justin-harper-como-refuerzo-de-los-indios/ |access-date=September 10, 2023 |website=magazine-pr.com |language=es}}</ref>

On August 25, 2020, Harper signed with [[Kyoto Hannaryz]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ジャスティン・ハーパー選手 加入のお知らせ |url=https://hannaryz.jp/news/detail/id=15681 |publisher=京都ハンナリーズ |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=25 August 2020}}</ref> On June 16, 2021, Harper re-signed with Kyoto Hannaryz.<ref>{{cite web |title=ジャスティン・ハーパー選手 契約合意のお知らせ |url=https://hannaryz.jp/news/detail/id=16941 |publisher=京都ハンナリーズ |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=16 June 2021}}</ref> On July 1, 2022, Harper signed with [[Koshigaya Alphas]] of the B.League.<ref>{{cite web |title=#32 ジャスティン・ハーパー 選手 2022-23シーズン選手契約(新規)のお知らせ |url=https://www.koshigaya-alphas.com/news/detail/id=45990 |publisher=越谷アルファーズ |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=1 July 2022}}</ref> On May 29, 2023, Harper re-signed with Koshigaya Alphas.<ref>{{cite web |title=#32 ジャスティン・ハーパー 選手 2023-24シーズン選手契約(継続)のお知らせ |url=https://www.koshigaya-alphas.com/news/202324s_32harper |publisher=越谷アルファーズ |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=29 May 2023}}</ref> On September 18, 2024, Harper signed with [[Fighting Eagles Nagoya]] of the B.League.<ref>{{cite web |title=【#32 ジャスティン・ハーパー 選手】新規入団のお知らせ |url=https://www.fightingeagles.jp/news/detail/id=16633 |publisher=ファイティングイーグルス名古屋 |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=18 September 2024}}</ref> On November 15, Harper left Fighting Eagles Nagoya.<ref>{{cite web |title=【#32 ジャスティン・ハーパー 選手】退団のお知らせ |url=https://www.fightingeagles.jp/news/detail/id=16742 |publisher=ファイティングイーグルス名古屋 |access-date=16 November 2024 |date=15 November 2024}}</ref>
